translations.text: i.e. of the Godhead.
i.e. besides that he is the Father.
i.e. it is for this that he has loved us.
i.e. it is from long ago that it has been determined for us that we should be sons by choice, not by nature.
i.e. he has granted it to us and has filled us with the grace of the Spirit.
i.e. for we were in bondage.
i.e. through the historical blood which flowed from his side when he was on the cross, and through the spiritual blood which is offered every day upon the altar.
i.e. for we deserved nothing but punishment.
i.e. it is all the more abundantly that he has bestowed it on us.
i.e. the inheritance of good deeds.
i.e. so that we might understand it.
i.e. the mystery of our salvation.
i.e. according to the good will.
i.e. until the time should come that was fitting for it.
i.e. it is long since that was prepared for us.
i.e. through the prophets, that it would come to us.
sealed
i.e. there is a sign upon them, i.e. the Holy Spirit.
i.e. that is a sign of our redemption and of our salvation.
i.e. not for any other work.
i.e. this is what I pray, i.e. that you may attain knowledge of God, and that the darkness of the worldly desires may not come over the eye of your soul.
i.e. so that the eye of your soul may be keen.
i.e. glory for us like the glory of God.
i.e. it was not fitting for him to be in that company, i.e. of the dead.
i.e. it was not merely on a visit [?] that he went.

i.e. he gives this: that all powers were under his feet in heaven and on earth; others [say] in the heavenly grades only. And it would not be impossible that there should be differences among these, so that each grade should be nobler than another, as it is in earthly grades.
i.e. above every name that is named.
i.e. the saints and the righteous, they are his body: Christ is the head, the saints are the body.
i.e. many gifts are not [given] to one man, and not one gift to a multitude.
i.e. they did not merit it.
Unbelieving ones [?], or despairing ones, who have despaired of their salvation through the passion of Christ.
i.e. as Christ works in the righteous, as Paul says, 'who works in us', so also the devil works in the children of distrust. These are sons by deed, then, and not sons by nature.
i.e. he did not bring us [?] for freedom.
i.e. not from the nature of the first creation, but from the nature of sin, which we have inherited from Adam.
i.e. he pitied us for being under the yoke of sin.
i.e. as Christ was raised up.
i.e. it is in Christ that we shall be after going thither.
i.e. it is by his grace that he has saved us, and not by merits.
i.e. in three ways, i.e. he has preached them, he has fulfilled them, he has granted them to us so that we may do them.
i.e. Israelite.
i.e. it was not circumcision of vices that they had, but circumcision of the flesh.
[You] were not people of the household.
i.e. of the law and of prophecy.
i.e. you are not guests or strangers now.
i.e. so after the coming of Christ the wall that was between God and man has been destroyed, i.e. sin, and [the wall] that was between bodies and souls.
i.e. while he was in the flesh.
i.e. the commandments of the law.
i.e. through the bestowing of the gifts of the Spirit on everyone.
i.e. the Spirit has been given to us all for our sanctification.
i.e. you are people of the household now.
i.e. the apostles, then, first came into the building, and the prophets after that. Christ, then, is the city of the saints who are united in Christ; they are the citizens (ciues).
i.e. the corner-stone there is Jesus Christ, i.e. sides and ends are held together in it, etc.
i.e. the assembly of the saints is called a temple, because Christ dwells in them.
i.e. a dwelling for God there.
i.e. you are a dwelling for God now.
Because I preach to you, that is what is laid to my charge.
as
i.e. so that you may understand it.
Or: though it be little that you take from my wisdom (a prudentia mea).
i.e. in the preaching of the gospel of Christ.
i.e. to the preachers (preceptoribus).
i.e. this is what was revealed to them.
i.e. united in the body of Christ.
i.e. of the mysteries (misteriorum): because they are united in the body of Christ, they will be in the glory that has been given to him.
i.e. through fulfilling the gospel.
i.e. it is in preaching the gospel that I am.
i.e. it is the grace of God that has come upon me, not my own merit.
Jews and Gentiles (iudeos et gentes), i.e. so that they might understand it.

i.e. the mystery of the salvation of the human race, and the gifts of the Holy Spirit to them, which had been hidden in the mysteries of the divinity (in the secrets of the Godhead); and even the household of heaven did not know it until the apostles revealed it to them, i.e. to the believers of the New Testament and to the household of heaven.
i.e. in the Church.

i.e. he means by these names only (tantum) all the heavenly ranks (pro omnibus gradibus caelestibus), for the household of heaven did not know the mysteries of the incarnation until they were revealed through the apostles, as it is said: 'Who is this King of glory?' Otherwise (aliter), these stand for all the ranks of the Church of the New Testament to whom the apostles preached.
i.e. their way of life, as in 'our conversation [is in heaven]' (ut nostra conuersatio), etc. Or: in the heavenly things (in donis caelestibus).
i.e. it is from afar that he has called.
i.e. do not let it be a disgrace in your eyes that I am in tribulations, for that is glory for you.
i.e. every creature that is called by the name of father in heaven and on earth has it from the Father.
i.e. that the image of the Spirit may be upon you
i.e. may it have been planted and may it have been founded, for they are planted [?]
i.e. as you have come to it [?]

i.e. in the mysteries of the Godhead is this fourfoldness, and in the cross of Christ; or the four virtues of the soul, i.e. of knowledge of the incarnation of Christ or of his divinity. The right hand of Christ saved the left of the world; his left hand saved the right part; the head redeemed the east, the feet the west.
i.e. what he does is more than what we ask
i.e. even that which we do not pray for
i.e. since he has set out the mystery of the salvation of the human race and what God has done for them, he then says afterwards that they should repay him with good [?]
i.e. patience from everyone toward another
i.e. though the turning [?] is threefold
i.e. a free gift
i.e. as God thought fit for each one
i.e. this is what he aims at
i.e. 'ascended' has been said of him
though
i.e. it is for this reason that 'ascended' is said of him
though it is he
i.e. for the many [?]
i.e. soul-friends
i.e. for perfecting, i.e. so that everyone may be perfect in the works of the ministry of the church
i.e. this is what comes of it: through the abundance of the gifts, in the multitude of the persons
i.e. that we may do what he has done
i.e. since it is perfect [?]; for the limb that does not fit with the body is not beautiful
i.e. since you have received [?] this from the apostles
i.e. from every [?]
i.e. remedy, i.e. everyone is wonderful [?] to them in disputing, so that they say: 'it is no easier for us than for everyone else'
i.e. it is fitting for the members to grow from the head.
i.e. each member from another.
i.e. of the grace that has been given to everyone.
i.e. I testify, i.e. I beseech.
i.e. it is 'est' indeed [?].
i.e. [?] (anicc).
i.e. besides, you have heard [?] (asné).
i.e. be righteous, because you are united in Christ, as he is righteous.
i.e. the mass of the old sins, or Adam with his deeds.
i.e. because you consent to them.
i.e. the mass of the virtues, or Christ with his works.
i.e. through the Holy Spirit; this man is spiritual.
i.e. this is its [?] (aimthuge).
i.e. because you are new men.
[?] ... because you are members.
i.e. against your sins, so that they may not be with you.
i.e. otherwise: this, then, is the fruit of your anger: to be without sin.
i.e. Christ, i.e. for he is not in a vessel of anger, or of discretion.
i.e. his coming into the heart in place of God.
i.e. let him not steal [?] from God, or simply.
i.e. if he has stolen anything, let him give something in its place to the poor from his labour.
i.e. for as man was formed in the image of God in the beginning, so he has now been formed in the image of the Spirit.
i.e. what each has done against another.
i.e. because you are members of Christ and you are a body to him.
i.e. great was the love, so that he went onto the cross for us, as he says: 'he gave himself up' etc.
i.e. a liquid offering, i.e. for blood
i.e. the fragrance of that offering filled the whole world and heaven
i.e. let it not be merely that it should not exist, etc.
i.e. not to think of crimes: that is a sign of perfect people
[?] (of baseness?)
i.e. those things are not [?] (fitting?) for perfect people
[?] (buffoonery?)
i.e. to profit
i.e. every kind of lust
i.e. because of the greatness of the sins and because of the likeness of the service that is done to them
i.e. beside [?] (the point)
i.e. though someone should say, 'You will have heaven though you do these things,' it will not be true
i.e. faciente, or [?]
i.e. pleasing
i.e. do not be in fellowship with them, for there is fruit for the works of light, i.e. eternal rewards; but there is nothing in these except what is unfruitful
i.e. he who has called you will bring them
i.e. he who rises through preaching, he is a preacher after his repentance
i.e. so that you may be light, as Christ is light
i.e. do not walk without looking about you
i.e. without penance, and not to do good
i.e. wise
i.e. drink abundantly of this
i.e. let everyone teach another, or pray diligently
i.e. for the man is a member of Christ, and the woman is a member of the man

i.e. this, then, is his custom: first to correct the women and put them under the power of their husbands, so that the husbands may be readier to be under the power of God, so that afterwards the men are corrected and offered to God's will; he does likewise in the case of servants and masters and of sons and fathers
i.e. so the union of Christ and the Church is undefiled; it is fitting that it should be so for everyone.
i.e. women are to be subject to the husband; the husband, however, is to love the women.
i.e. as the Church is a body to Christ, so the woman is a body to the man.
as it is
i.e. his body is not [?] to him.
i.e. the cherishing of it is evident in us.
i.e. because it is to Christ and to the Church that it is fitting.
i.e. for the member is of the body.
let the husband love the wife, let the wife fear the husband
i.e. the whole household is included, so that there may be no damage to the union of the Church.
i.e. it is right.
i.e. teach.
i.e. so that they may be more obedient to God, to the commands of the Lord God.
i.e. for he is present to his servants; they do nothing that he will not know.
i.e. willingly.
i.e. let the service be of free will.
i.e. do not, then, [?] your power.
i.e. you have one Lord.
i.e. 'tempore' from here onward.
i.e. in the example and in the power of the Lord; God will help you.
a repetition
i.e. take the armour of God upon you to fight against the devil.
i.e. nothing else is needed but only to resist, as it is said: 'Resist the devil and he will flee from you.'
i.e. so that they might have arms of the flesh.
i.e. because you are in battle, or because your wrestling is not against flesh, let it be the armour of God that you have, and not any other arms.
i.e. only let the armour of God be upon you
i.e. a girdle of truth about you
i.e. peace between God and man, etc.
i.e. that you may ward off, i.e. [?]
i.e. that will be salvation for you
i.e. that you may obtain that sword
i.e. let the prayer be spiritual
i.e. in every perseverance
constantly
i.e. that you may obtain that spiritual thing
i.e. let it not be for yourselves alone
i.e. this is what is dearer to me: the grace of preaching
i.e. of the opening for preaching
i.e. without hindrance
i.e. it is for the preaching that I am in chains
i.e. worthily, as well as it may be preached
i.e. so that you may know that there are bonds upon me
i.e. whether there is deliverance for me or not
i.e. it is for this that he has been sent
i.e. because many believe in God through my preaching
i.e. they are the treasures of a dutiful son
